kpsea-science-2023.subject: Integrated Science
instructions: You have 1 hour 20 minutes to complete this paper.
Read each question carefully before answering.

sectionA.questionText: During a lesson, Grade 6 learners discussed functions of different parts of a plant. Which part of a plant is responsible for making plant food?
sectionA.explanation:
The leaf is the primary site of photosynthesis, the process by which a plant makes its food.

* Roots absorb water and minerals, the stem transports these materials and supports the plant, and the fruit protects seeds.
* None of these other parts are the primary site of food production.

sectionA.questionText:
The following diagrams were drawn by learners to represent two types of root systems E and F.
Which one of the following pairs of plants is matched to its correct root system.
sectionA.explanation:
Diagram E shows a tap root system (one main thick root with smaller lateral roots), while Diagram F shows a fibrous root system (many roots of similar size growing from the stem base).

* Beans are dicotyledons and have tap roots (E).
* Maize is a monocotyledon and has fibrous roots (F).

sectionA.questionText: During a class activity, learners recorded the following observations about a group of invertebrates:
questionList: (i) three body parts;
(ii) three pairs of legs;
(iii) have wings;
(iv) have antennae.
sectionA.questionSuffix: Which one of the following is a member of the group observed by the learners?
sectionA.explanation:
The characteristics listed (three body parts, three pairs of legs, wings, and antennae) describe insects.

* A cockroach is an insect.
* A tick is an arachnid (two body parts, four pairs of legs), while millipedes and centipedes are myriapods with many body segments and numerous legs.

sectionA.questionText:
The following diagram represents some parts of the human heart drawn by learners during a lesson on functions of parts of the heart.
Which one of the following is a function of the part labelled G?

options.text: Pumping blood to other parts of the body.
Receiving blood from the rest of the body.

sectionA.explanation:
The part labelled G is the left ventricle, which is characterized by its thick muscular wall.

* Its function is to pump oxygenated blood with high pressure to all other parts of the body.
* Pumping blood to the lungs is the job of the right ventricle, while receiving blood is the job of the atria (upper chambers).

sectionA.questionText: Grade 6 learners listed the following parts of the human reproductive system. Which part belongs to the female reproductive system?
sectionA.explanation:
The cervix is the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina, making it a part of the female reproductive system.

* The prostate, testis, and penis are all parts of the male reproductive system.

sectionA.questionText: During a Science lesson, learners observed activities shown in the following pictures. In which one of the activities is water **not** conserved?
sectionA.explanation:
Activity D shows a person washing a car using a running hosepipe, which wastes a lot of water.

* In contrast, harvesting rainwater (A), mulching to retain soil moisture (B), and using a cup while brushing teeth (C) are all excellent methods of conserving water.

sectionA.questionText: A person donated a desktop computer to a friend who needed it instead of throwing it away. This is an example of managing solid waste by
sectionA.explanation:
Giving an item to someone else to use in its current form is 'reusing'.

* **'Recycling'** would involve breaking down the computer to make a new product, and 'reducing' involves buying less in the first place.
* Therefore, this action is reusing only.

sectionA.questionText: During a class discussion, learners suggested ways of controlling water pollution. Which one of the following ways would control water pollution?
sectionA.explanation:
Avoiding open defecation prevents harmful human waste from being washed into rivers and lakes, thereby controlling water pollution at its source.

* Boiling, filtration, and chemical treatment are methods of purifying water *after* it has already been polluted or drawn for use, not ways of controlling the pollution itself.

sectionA.questionText: During a class discussion, learners listed ways of preventing infestation by external parasites. Which one of the following ways prevent infestation by jiggers?
sectionA.explanation:
Jiggers are external parasites found in dust and soil that burrow into bare feet or toes.

* Wearing shoes protects the feet and prevents jiggers from entering the skin.
* Not sharing clothes, soaking clothes, and ironing are methods used to prevent lice or bedbugs, not jiggers.

sectionA.questionText:
Learners used a ball and ring shown in the following set up to demonstrate a certain property of matter. They observed that the ball could pass through the ring before heating but after heating it could not.
Which one of the following properties of matter was being demonstrated? Matter
sectionA.explanation:
Heating the metal ball caused it to increase in size (expand) so it could no longer fit through the ring.

* When it cools, it will decrease in size (contract) and fit through again.
* This classic experiment specifically demonstrates that solid matter expands when heated and contracts when cooled.

sectionA.questionText: Which one of the statements describes an application of change of state of matter in everyday life?
sectionA.explanation:
Drying clothes involves evaporation, where liquid water in the wet clothes changes its state into water vapor (gas) and escapes into the air.

* Working of thermometers involves expansion, warming water is a temperature change without a state change, and hardening of bricks is a chemical/structural change.

sectionA.questionText: Which one of the following components of air is 78% by volume?
sectionA.explanation:
Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, making up approximately 78% by volume.

* Oxygen makes up about 21%, while carbon dioxide and inert gases (like argon) make up less than 1% combined.

sectionA.questionText: Learners listed the following as ways by which friction can be reduced. Which one was **not** correct?
sectionA.explanation:
Sharpening tools is a way of increasing pressure to cut objects easily, it does not reduce friction between moving parts.

* In contrast, lubrication (oiling), smoothening rough surfaces, and using rollers (or ball bearings) are all effective methods used specifically to reduce friction.

sectionA.questionText: A learner used a ladder as a simple machine to reach and fix a bulb in a house. The ladder is a simple machine because it makes it easier to

options.text: overcome loads in the opposite direction of force

sectionA.explanation:
A ladder acts as an inclined plane, which is a simple machine that makes it easier to move loads (like a person) upwards through heights.

* It does not move loads horizontally, in circles, or in opposite directions (which describes a pulley).

sectionA.questionText: Learners observed a cloud which appeared long, curled, feather-like and light. The cloud observed is most likely to be
sectionA.explanation:
Cirrus clouds are high-altitude clouds that are characterized by their thin, wispy, curled, and feather-like appearance.

* Nimbus clouds are dark rain clouds, stratus clouds are flat featureless layers, and cumulus clouds are large, puffy, cotton-like clouds.

sectionA.questionText:
The following photograph shows a farmer constructing a structure for controlling soil erosion. Study it and answer questions 16 and 17.
Identify the structure in the picture.
sectionA.explanation:
The farmer is constructing a stepped ridge along the contour of a slope, which is a terrace.

* A gabion is a wire mesh box filled with stones, a grass strip is a planted band of grass, and a trash line is a pile of dry vegetation.

sectionA.questionText: How does the structure control soil erosion?
sectionA.explanation:
Terraces work primarily by breaking a long slope into a series of shorter, flatter steps.

* This effectively reduces the speed of surface runoff water, preventing it from washing away the topsoil.
* While it can also hold soil back, reducing the speed of water is the fundamental mechanism of terracing.
* Intercepting raindrops is the role of vegetation cover.

sectionA.questionText:
The picture below shows farm produce labelled 'ORGANIC' on the market.
What does the label 'ORGANIC' mean? The farm produce is
sectionA.explanation:
In agriculture, the term 'organic' refers to produce that has been grown without the use of artificial fertilizers, synthetic pesticides, or other synthetic chemicals.

* It does not necessarily mean it is free from pests (though farmers use natural methods), nor does it automatically mean it is fresher or tastier than conventionally grown produce.

sectionA.questionText:
The following photograph shows a method of protecting livestock. Use it to answer questions 19 and 20.
The method protects the livestock by

options.text: preventing entry of the wild animals

sectionA.explanation:
The photograph shows a physical fence or boma surrounding the livestock.

* This physical barrier works by preventing the entry of predators and wild animals.
* It does not produce flashing lights, actively scare animals (like a scarecrow), or trap them.

sectionA.questionText: How can you describe the animals in the photograph? They are
sectionA.explanation:
The animals in the photograph are goats and sheep.

* Goats and sheep are ruminants that feed exclusively on plant matter (grass and leaves), which makes them herbivores.
* Carnivores eat meat, omnivores eat both meat and plants, and decomposers break down dead matter.

sectionA.questionText:
The following photograph shows a farmer carrying out a practice after germination of maize. Study it and answer questions 21 to 23.
Identify the practice.
sectionA.explanation: The practice is gapping, which involves planting new seeds or seedlings in spaces where the original seeds failed to germinate, ensuring a full crop stand.

sectionA.questionText: Which one of the following wild animals most likely interferes with germination of seeds?
sectionA.explanation:
Squirrels are known to dig up and eat planted seeds like maize before or during germination, directly interfering with the process.

* Moles primarily damage roots, monkeys eat mature fruits or cobs, and weaver birds are notorious pests for mature cereal grains (like wheat or sorghum heads) rather than germinating seeds.

sectionA.questionText: From the photograph, name the other caring practice the farmer carried out on the maize.
sectionA.explanation:
In the photograph, while the farmer is uprooting excess maize plants (thinning), they are also simultaneously clearing the surrounding soil of unwanted plants.

* This secondary caring practice is weed control.
* The maize plants are far too young for harvesting or pruning, and maize does not require training.

sectionA.questionText: Which one of the following is an indigenous vegetable crop?
sectionA.explanation:
Pigweed (Amaranthus, commonly known as Terere) is an indigenous African leafy vegetable.

* Cabbage, kales (sukuma wiki), and spinach are all exotic vegetables that were introduced from other parts of the world.

sectionA.questionText: Which one of the following pairs of crops consists of indigenous root crops?
sectionA.explanation:
Cassava and arrowroots (nduma) are considered traditional or indigenous root and tuber crops heavily cultivated in local farming.

* Carrots and beetroots are exotic root crops that were introduced from temperate regions.

sectionA.questionText: Grade 5 learners at Kabila primary school were asked to give the meaning of common communicable diseases. Which one of the following statements is true about common communicable diseases?

options.text: They are diseases that are spread easily from one person to another.
They are diseases that cannot be spread from one person to another.
They are diseases that are spread only by communicating to people.
They are diseases that spread only when people move from one place to another.

sectionA.explanation:
Communicable diseases are illnesses caused by infectious agents (like viruses or bacteria) that can be easily transmitted from one infected person (or animal) to another.

* They are not spread by 'communicating' verbally, nor do they only spread when people move places, as they can spread within a household.
* Non-communicable diseases are the ones that cannot be spread (like diabetes or cancer).

sectionA.questionText:
Four Grade 6 learners were asked by their teacher to bring some items needed for a Home Science lesson. Below is what each learner brought:
Auma: Body lotion, petroleum jelly and skin care cream.
Chris: Thread, thimble, make-up kit and pins.
Fatma: Tie, socks, belt and scarf.
Festus: Cup, spoon, perfume and needle.
Who among the learners brought accessories used to enhance personal appearance?
sectionA.explanation:
In Home Science, accessories are items worn with garments to complete or enhance an outfit.

* Ties, socks, belts, and scarves are all clothing accessories.
* Auma brought cosmetics/lotions, Chris brought sewing equipment (plus makeup), and Festus brought utensils and perfume.

sectionA.questionText: Razia advised her parents to always include savings in their family budget. Which one of the following statements is true about savings?

options.text: Savings is the amount of money you are left with after buying all items required.
Savings is the amount of money you are given back after paying for items.
Savings is the amount of money set aside for unexpected expenses.
Savings is the amount of money set aside for future use.

sectionA.explanation:
Savings is a deliberate decision to set aside a portion of income for future use or goals.

* Money set aside specifically for unexpected expenses is usually called an 'emergency fund'.
* Money left over after buying things is just a balance, and money given back after paying is 'change'.

sectionA.questionText: Masiero accompanied her father to the shop to buy cooking fat. Which one of the following is an important factor they should consider when choosing the cooking fat?
sectionA.explanation:
The expiry date is crucial for health and safety, as it indicates whether the cooking fat is still safe for consumption.

* Consuming expired products can cause food poisoning.
* The color, type, or weight of the packaging material are secondary factors that do not affect the safety or quality of the food inside.

sectionA.questionText: Grade 5 learners were asked to identify micronutrients found in food. Some of the micronutrients they identified are
sectionA.explanation:
Micronutrients are essential elements required by organisms in varying, but small, quantities throughout life (hence 'micro').

* Vitamins and minerals fall into this category.
* Proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids (fats) are macronutrients because the body requires them in large amounts.

sectionA.questionText: Lotum has advised his uncle not to use salting method to preserve meat. Which one of the following is a reason Lotum's uncle should avoid using salt to preserve meat?

options.text: Salt decreases the risk of asthma.

sectionA.explanation:
Excessive consumption of salt (sodium) is a major dietary risk factor for developing hypertension (high blood pressure) and heart disease.

* It does not increase the risk of constipation, nor does it improve weak bones or decrease asthma risks.

sectionA.questionText: Salim is suffering from scurvy. Which one of the following eating habits is likely to have made Salim to develop scurvy?

options.text: Decreased consumption of fruits and vegetables.
Increased consumption of fruits and vegetables.
Decreased consumption of foods rich in carbohydrates.
Increased consumption of foods rich in fibre and water.

sectionA.explanation:
Scurvy is a nutritional deficiency disease caused by a severe lack of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) in the diet.

* Vitamin C is abundantly found in fresh fruits (especially citrus) and vegetables.
* Therefore, a decreased consumption of these foods leads to scurvy.

sectionA.questionText: Ann and Ken were talking about one of the steps in laundering a handkerchief. The handkerchief is put in clean cold salty water without soap for some time. The step they were talking about is
sectionA.explanation:
Soaking involves placing an item in water (often with salt to dissolve mucus in handkerchiefs or blood stains) for a period of time before the actual washing begins.

* This loosens dirt.
* Washing involves soap and agitation, rinsing removes soap, and sorting is separating clothes before laundering.

sectionA.questionText: Amanda has noticed that her school uniform has a gaping seam. She wants to repair it. Which one of the following stitches can she use to repair the gaping seam?
sectionA.explanation:
A back stitch is a very strong, permanent stitch used to join two pieces of fabric together, making it perfect for repairing a torn or gaping seam.

* Hemming is used to finish raw edges (like the bottom of a skirt), oversewing is for neatening raw edges to prevent fraying, and loop stitches are often decorative or used for buttonholes.

sectionA.questionText: Every time Rihana wears her favourite dress, it clings to the body which makes her uncomfortable. To prevent the dress from clinging to her body, Rihana should

options.text: rinse the dress well with clean water
use a fabric conditioner when rinsing.

sectionA.explanation:
Clothes clinging to the body is usually caused by static electricity built up in synthetic fabrics.

* Fabric conditioners (softeners) coat the fibers with a lubricating layer that reduces friction and static cling.
* Bleach removes stains, disinfectants kill germs, and clean water removes soap, but none of these stop static cling.

sectionA.questionText: Grade 6 learners developed the following rules for racing games:
questionList: i. Wear suitable shoes while running;
ii. Keep to your lane when running;
iii. Drink adequate amount of water before the race;
iv. Avoid performing any exercise before the race.
sectionA.questionSuffix: Which one of the following set of rules is correct?
sectionA.explanation:
Rules i, ii, and iii are all correct safety and performance guidelines for racing.

* However, rule 'iv' is completely wrong—athletes *must* perform warm-up exercises before a race to prepare their muscles and prevent injuries.
* Therefore, only the set containing i, ii, and iii is correct.

sectionA.questionText: Rope skipping is a common physical activity. Which one of the following statement is true about the effects of rope skipping exercise?
sectionA.explanation:
Rope skipping is a cardiovascular exercise that strengthens the heart, improves lung capacity, tones muscles, and improves overall physical fitness.

* While poor technique *could* hurt ankles, the general and primary intended effect is improving fitness.
* It actively prevents lifestyle diseases and strengthens (rather than weakens) leg joints over time.

sectionA.questionText: Grade 6 learners were asked to run to a specific point within the shortest time possible. Which component of fitness were the learners developing?
sectionA.explanation:
Running to a specific point in the *shortest time possible* is a direct measure and training method for speed (the ability to move the body or a part of it rapidly over a distance).

* Strength is about exerting force, balance is about maintaining stability, and coordination is about smooth, controlled movements.

sectionA.questionText: Sharing food during a camping activity is common among a group of friends. Why should friends share food during an outdoor activity?

options.text: Show friends' background with different kinds of food.
Promote unity among friends for better group work.
Encourage friends to rely on others for food.
Saves time for those who do not want to prepare and carry food.

sectionA.explanation:
Sharing food promotes social cohesion, teamwork, and unity among campers.

* Outdoor activities heavily rely on group work and a sense of community, rather than showing off or encouraging dependency.

sectionA.questionText: During an outdoor activity, a group of learners found the following sign marked on the path.
sectionA.explanation: The arrow in the sign points to the right, indicating a path or instruction to turn right.

sectionA.questionText: A gymnastic competitor performed the skill shown in the following picture.
sectionA.questionSuffix: What is the name of the gymnastic skill?
sectionA.explanation: The image shows a competitor performing a side vault, characterized by one hand supporting the body while vaulting sideways.

sectionA.questionText: A first aid box contains items that are used when one is injured. Which of the following items is correctly matched with its use during first aid?

options.text: Scissors - cutting papers and muscles that have been injured.
Bandages - making straps to support the first aid box.
Cotton wool - applying antiseptics and cleaning cuts.

sectionA.explanation:
Cotton wool is correctly matched; it is used to clean wounds and apply antiseptics.

* Scissors are used to cut bandages (not muscles!), bandages are used to secure dressings, and a thermometer measures (but does not control) body temperature.

sectionA.questionText: Learners improvised relay batons using various materials. Which of the following material made the most durable relay baton?
sectionA.explanation: Wood is the strongest and most resilient material among the options provided, making it the most durable for improvising a relay baton that can survive being dropped and passed.

sectionA.questionText: The following picture shows a gymnast performing a
sectionA.explanation: The gymnast is supporting their entire body weight vertically on their hands alone, which is known as a hand stand.

sectionA.questionText: Four learners set up outdoor shelters as follows:
questionList: Jane: Close to the river
John: At the top of the hill
James: At the bottom of the valley
Juliet: At a gentle slope sheltered by trees
sectionA.questionSuffix: Who among the learners chose a suitable site for an outdoor shelter?
sectionA.explanation:
Juliet chose the best site.

* A gentle slope allows for proper water drainage, and trees provide natural shelter from strong winds and harsh sun.
* Valleys and riversides are prone to flooding and cold, while the top of a hill exposes the shelter to strong winds.

sectionA.questionText: Two players collided during a PHE lesson. One player started bleeding from the nose. Which one of the following is the correct first aid to control the bleeding?

options.text: Lying on the back while facing up.
Putting cotton wool in the nostrils to block the blood from flowing.
Sitting while leaning forward and pinching the soft part of the nose.
Sitting down with legs raised to relax and stop bleeding.

sectionA.explanation: For a nosebleed, the victim should sit up and lean slightly forward (so blood drains out, not down the throat) and pinch the soft part of the nose to apply pressure and help the blood clot.

sectionA.questionText: Learners were asked to improvise a triangular bandage. Which one of the following material was suitable for improvising the bandage?
sectionA.explanation:
A triangular bandage is primarily made from fabric.

* Pieces of old clothes can easily be cut into a triangular shape and are soft, flexible, and strong enough to support injured limbs, unlike paper, leaves, or carton.

sectionA.questionText: Learners were asked to improvise a soccer ball to use during the inter-class competition. Which of the following materials did the learners use?
sectionA.explanation: According to the curriculum, a combination of soft materials like cotton wool, papers, and strings can be used to improvise a safe and functional soccer ball for physical education.

sectionA.questionText: A school handball team members took their positions in the court ready to start the game. How many players did the team comprise?
sectionA.explanation: A standard handball team consists of 7 players on the court at any one time (6 outfield players and 1 goalkeeper).

sectionA.questionText: When starting a race in athletics, competitors are given commands. Which of the following command is not given?
sectionA.explanation:
The standard starting commands for a sprint race are 'On your marks', 'Set', and 'Go' (which is often a starting pistol).

* **'Run'** is not used as a starting command.

ctx-eng-q13-15.title:
Questions 13 to 15
Read the story below and then answer questions 13 to 15.
ctx-eng-q13-15.text:
Many afternoons, Hyena and Hare spent hours in a field eating the farmer's groundnuts. One day, Hare heard that the farmer was complaining that his groundnuts were being stolen. Hare went to him and said, "I will catch the thief for you."

One afternoon, Hare told Hyena that groundnuts are sweeter when you eat them with your legs buried in the ground. Hyena buried his four legs in the ground. He looked at the Hare and asked him, "Hare, why have you not buried your four legs?" Hare replied, "My legs are very short." Hyena was happy with Hare's answer, and he continued eating groundnuts. Hare watched carefully and when he saw the farmer coming, he quickly ran away. Hyena too saw the farmer, and tried to escape, but his legs were stuck in the ground. The farmer caught him and gave him a thorough beating.

ctx-eng-q10-12.title:
Questions 10 to 12
Read the story below and then answer questions 10 to 12.
ctx-eng-q10-12.text:
Hassan likes running errands for his parents. The other day, he was sent to the shop to buy some items. His father had written the prices of the items on a list. The total cost was four hundred and twenty five shillings. His father had given him five hundred shillings. Hassan was expecting a balance of seventy five shillings.

The shopkeeper was very busy on that day. She was serving many customers. When Hassan got the balance, he stepped out of the shop to count the money. He could not believe it. The shopkeeper had given him five hundred and seventy five shillings! Hassan thought this was his lucky day.

He sat down under a tree to plan how he would spend his new found cash. He started counting all the things he wanted to buy. This time he would go to a different shop.

On his way to the shop, Hassan remembered what his father had once told him, "Never take what does not belong to you". He realised the five hundred shillings belonged to the shopkeeper. He walked back to the shop to return the money. The shopkeeper was surprised to see him back so soon. When Hassan handed her the money, she was very grateful and said, "You are an angel. I'm proud of you, young man".

Hassan walked home shoulder high. He knew his father would be very pleased with him.

ctx-eng-q6-9.title:
Questions 6 to 9
Read the passage below and then answer questions 6 to 9.
ctx-eng-q6-9.text:
Human beings have always kept animals for different purposes. Animals can be kept as pets. A pet is an animal kept for pleasure. We keep pets because we love their company. We play with them. They are just like our friends, so we keep them happy and comfortable. Indeed, the dog, which is a common pet, has been said to be man's best friend.

Animals can also be kept to help human beings do certain tasks. This is because they have **special** abilities which human beings do not have. For example, donkeys have strength to carry heavy luggage. They can therefore help us in transportation.

Some animals are kept as source of food. Animal products such as milk and eggs are a rich source of nutrients. It is important to realise that whether we keep animals as pets, to help in work, or for food, they deserve kind treatment.

ctx-eng-q1-3.title:
Questions 1 to 3
Read the telephone conversation below. It contains blank spaces numbered 1 to 3. For each blank space, select the best alternative from the choices given.
ctx-eng-q1-3.text:
**Pupil:** Hello, Teacher.

**Class teacher:** Hello, ----1----.

**Pupil:** I am Barasa Kabengi, a pupil in Grade 6 Yellow.

**Class teacher:** Yes, Barasa, how can I help you?

**Pupil:** ----2----.

**Class teacher:** Is there a problem at home?

**Pupil:** My young sister is joining Grade 1 today. She has been crying. She wants me to accompany her to school. Grade 1 learners are to report at 8:30 a.m. today.

**Class teacher:** Okay, Barasa. You can come along with her. Make sure you come to see me after she settles down in her classroom.

**Pupil:** ----3----.

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 1:

options.text: Whom do you want to speak to?

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
In polite telephone etiquette and formal English grammar, when asking for the identity of the person on the other end of the line, we use the objective pronoun 'whom' because it acts as the object of the preposition 'to' (*To whom am I speaking?* or *Whom am I speaking to?*).

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Whom am I speaking to?** is correct because it uses the polite, objective pronoun 'whom' to ask for the recipient's identity in formal telephone communication.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Who are you?:** Blunt, demanding, and impolite for formal telephone conversations.
* **Who is this?:** Very informal and lacks the professional respect required when speaking to a teacher on the phone.
* **Whom do you want to speak to?:** Reverses the roles; the caller (pupil) is trying to confirm who answered the phone, not asking the teacher who they want to talk to.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use formal, polite phrasing like "Whom am I speaking to?" when inquiring about someone's identity on the phone.

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 2:

options.text: May I be late for school today?
I want to be late for school today.
I will be late for school today.
Must I be late for school today?

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
The modal auxiliary verb **May** is used in formal English to politely request permission from an authority figure (such as a teacher or parent).

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**May I be late for school today?** is correct because it uses 'May I...' to politely request the teacher's permission to arrive late due to helping his younger sister.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **I want to be late for school today.:** Expresses a personal desire rather than asking for permission politely.
* **I will be late for school today.:** A blunt, direct statement declaring a future action without seeking approval.
* **Must I be late for school today?:** Asks if being late is a compulsory obligation, which makes no sense in this context.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "May I..." when politely requesting permission from teachers, elders, or authority figures.

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 3:
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
In social dialogue etiquette, when someone in authority grants your request or offers assistance, the appropriate and courteous response is to express gratitude.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Thank you, Teacher.** is correct because Barasa must show gratitude after his class teacher grants him permission to accompany his sister.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **That's good, Teacher.:** Sounds casual and evaluative rather than showing personal appreciation.
* **It's okay, Teacher.:** Informal and sounds like reassuring the teacher instead of thanking them.
* **It's alright, Teacher.:** Casual expression used to accept an apology, not to thank someone for permission.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Always respond with "Thank you" when someone grants a request or helps you.

sectionA.questionText:
For questions 4 to 5, complete each of the blank spaces with the correct alternative from the choices given.

4. If I had a lot of money, I ------- travel all over the world.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
In English grammar, conditional sentences talk about real or imaginary situations. The Second Conditional is used for hypothetical or imaginary situations in the present/future: **If + past simple, ... would + base verb**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**would** is correct because "If I had a lot of money..." is an unreal/imaginary condition (Second Conditional), requiring **would travel**.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **should:** Used to give advice or state obligation, not to express hypothetical conditional results.
* **can:** Used for real present ability, whereas a past conditional clause (*had*) requires the past modal form (*would*).
* **will:** Used in First Conditional sentences (*If I have money, I will travel...*) for real future possibilities.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Second Conditional structure: *If + past simple (had), ... WOULD + main verb (travel)*.

sectionA.questionText: 5. Odoko goes to school ------- foot every morning.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Prepositions of travel and movement have specific rules in English. We say **by car**, **by bus**, **by train**, **by plane**, but when referring to walking, the set idiomatic phrase is strictly **on foot**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**on** is correct because the standard English preposition used with "foot" to mean walking is **on foot**.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **by:** Used for vehicles and modes of transport (e.g., *by bus*, *by car*), not for walking on your feet.
* **with:** Means using a tool or accompanying someone (e.g., *with a pen*), not for walking.
* **in:** Indicates being inside a vehicle (e.g., *in a taxi*), not walking on foot.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Always use "on foot" when referring to walking to a destination.

sectionA.questionText: 6. Why do we keep pets?

options.text: To help us carry heavy things.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Reading comprehension requires extracting direct facts stated in a text. Paragraph 1 of the passage explicitly defines a pet as an animal kept for pleasure and companionship.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**To make us happy.** is correct because the text states that pets are kept for pleasure, companionship, and to bring happiness to our lives.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **To help us carry heavy things.:** The passage states that donkeys are kept to carry heavy luggage (work animals), not pets.
* **To provide food.:** The passage notes that some livestock are kept as a source of food (milk and eggs), not pets.
* **To protect the environment.:** Environmental protection is not mentioned as a reason for keeping pets in the passage.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Pets are kept for pleasure and companionship ("to make us happy"), while work animals carry loads.

sectionA.questionText: 7. Which one of the following is **true** about donkeys and dogs?

options.text: They can do things that we cannot do.
They are always comfortable and healthy.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Comprehension questions ask learners to identify true statements based on the provided passage. Paragraph 2 mentions that animals have special abilities that human beings do not have (e.g., donkeys carrying heavy loads, dogs' acute senses).

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**They can do things that we cannot do.** is correct because the passage explicitly states that animals possess special abilities that human beings lack.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **They are man's best friend.:** The passage specifically mentions that the dog is man's best friend, not donkeys.
* **They are better than us.:** The text does not make a moral or general claim that animals are superior to humans.
* **They are always comfortable and healthy.:** The passage emphasizes that humans must care for animals to keep them comfortable, not that they are always healthy on their own.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Animals assist humans because they possess unique physical abilities that humans do not have.

sectionA.questionText: 8. The word **'special'** as used in the passage means the same as
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Vocabulary in context requires finding a synonym that fits the exact meaning of a word as used in a sentence. In the passage, "special abilities" means abilities that are exceptional, distinct, or out of the ordinary.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**unusual.** is correct because "special" refers to uncommon, extraordinary, or exceptional traits that set them apart.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **strange.:** Means odd or weird in a negative way, which does not match the positive context of special abilities.
* **new.:** Means recently made or acquired, not exceptional.
* **unknown.:** Means unfamiliar or obscure, which does not fit known animal abilities.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Contextual vocabulary: "special" in this context means exceptional or unusual abilities.

sectionA.questionText: 9. What is likely to happen if we do not treat animals kindly?

options.text: They will not live with us.
They may not give us enough food.
We may not get enough benefits from them.
We may not be happy and comfortable.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Making inferences based on text evidence requires looking at cause-and-effect relationships in the passage. The final paragraph emphasizes that treating animals kindly ensures they remain helpful and productive for us.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**We may not get enough benefits from them.** is correct because mistreating work animals, pets, or food source animals reduces their ability to serve, work, or produce for us.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **They will not live with us.:** Animals may remain captive even if mistreated, so this is not the main logical outcome.
* **They may not give us enough food.:** Applies only to food animals, whereas the passage covers pets, work animals, and food animals together.
* **We may not be happy and comfortable.:** Relates mainly to pets, not the broader practical benefits of all domestic animals.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Treating animals kindly ensures we receive maximum benefits, help, and companionship from them.

sectionA.questionText: 10. Why did Hassan's father write the list of items?

options.text: He did not want Hassan to forget any item.
He did not want Hassan to delay in the shop.
He wanted Hassan to get the right balance from the shopkeeper.
He wanted Hassan to do the totals of the cost of the items.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
In reading comprehension, identifying character motives requires analyzing the details given in the story. Paragraph 1 explains that Hassan's father wrote the item prices on a list so Hassan could calculate the correct expected balance.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**He wanted Hassan to get the right balance from the shopkeeper.** is correct because the story notes the father wrote down prices so Hassan knew he was expecting exactly 75 shillings balance.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **He did not want Hassan to forget any item.:** The list contained prices specifically to calculate the total cost and balance.
* **He did not want Hassan to delay in the shop.:** Saving time was not stated as the motive for listing prices.
* **He wanted Hassan to do the totals of the cost of the items.:** Hassan's main check at the shop was calculating his expected change/balance.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Writing down item prices helps buyers verify the total cost and calculate the exact change expected.

sectionA.questionText: 11. The shopkeeper was surprised to see Hassan back because ---------

options.text: the shopkeeper was very busy that day.
Hassan had just left the shop.
the shopkeeper had given him the balance.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Analyzing story details helps explain character reactions. The story states Hassan counted his money under a tree right outside the shop and immediately walked back when he realized the error.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Hassan had just left the shop.** is correct because Hassan returned almost immediately after stepping out, catching the shopkeeper by surprise.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Hassan returned the money.:** Returning money explained why she was grateful, but seeing him back so *soon* (just after leaving) is what surprised her.
* **the shopkeeper was very busy that day.:** Being busy explains why she made a mistake, not why she was surprised by Hassan's quick return.
* **the shopkeeper had given him the balance.:** Giving change was a routine transaction, not the cause of her surprise.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** The shopkeeper was surprised because Hassan returned almost immediately after leaving.

sectionA.questionText: 12. This story teaches us that ---------

options.text: a friend in need is a friend indeed.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
A fable or narrative lesson summarizes the moral story message. Hassan chose to return the extra 500 shillings because of his father's advice: "Never take what does not belong to you."

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**honesty is the best policy.** is correct because Hassan's honest decision earned him praise, self-respect, and a clean conscience.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **hurry hurry has no blessing.:** This proverb warns against rash speed, which is unrelated to returning stolen/extra money.
* **once bitten twice shy.:** Refers to learning from past bad experiences, not returning extra change.
* **a friend in need is a friend indeed.:** Refers to true friendship during difficult times, which does not fit the shopkeeper encounter.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Returning money that does not belong to you illustrates the classic moral: "Honesty is the best policy.

sectionA.questionText: 13. Which one of the following is **true** according to the story?

options.text: Hare stole the groundnuts just like Hyena.
Hare was a true friend of the farmer.
Hare was not able to cheat Hyena.
Hare buried one of his legs in the ground.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Story comprehension requires verifying factual accuracy against events in the narrative. In the story, both Hyena and Hare were eating the farmer's groundnuts without permission.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Hare stole the groundnuts just like Hyena.** is correct because both animals were illegally eating the farmer's crops in the field.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Hare was a true friend of the farmer.:** Hare was deceiving both the farmer and Hyena to avoid punishment.
* **Hare was not able to cheat Hyena.:** Hare successfully tricked Hyena into burying his legs in the soil.
* **Hare buried one of his legs in the ground.:** Hare lied that his legs were too short and did not bury any of his legs.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Both Hare and Hyena were crop thieves, but Hare tricked Hyena to save himself.

sectionA.questionText: 14. From the story, Hare is ---------.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Character traits are identified through a character's actions and dialogue. Hare tricked Hyena into burying his legs so Hare could escape while Hyena took the blame and got beaten.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**tricky** is correct because Hare used clever deceit and trickery to trap Hyena and escape unharmed.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **friendly:** Hare acted deceitfully towards Hyena, showing he was not a true friend.
* **funny:** While the trick was humorous, Hare's defining character trait in animal tales is being sly and tricky.
* **busy:** Hare was spending time stealing crops and plotting tricks, not engaged in productive work.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** In traditional folktales, Hare is portrayed as a cunning and tricky character.

sectionA.questionText: 15. What do we learn from this story?

options.text: People need to share what they have.
We should keep the right friends.
We should always do what we are told.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Moral themes highlight the broader life lessons learned from characters' mistakes. Hyena trusted Hare blindly despite Hare's suspicious actions, leading to Hyena getting caught and beaten.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**We should keep the right friends.** is correct because trusting a dishonest, tricky companion like Hare leads to betrayal and trouble.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **People need to share what they have.:** The story is about stealing and betrayal, not generous sharing.
* **Farmers should beat all Hyenas.:** Physical punishment of animals is not the intended moral lesson of the folktale.
* **We should always do what we are told.:** Blindly obeying bad advice (like Hyena burying his legs) leads to disaster.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Be cautious about who you trust; keeping untrustworthy friends leads to trouble.

sectionA.questionText: 16. Asha has a small garden at home. She likes it because it is a gift from ----16---- grandfather.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Possessive adjectives show ownership. Since "Asha" is a female person (she/her), the corresponding possessive adjective for a singular female owner is **her**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**her** is correct because Asha is female, making "her grandfather" the grammatically correct possessive form.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **his:** Possessive adjective used for a male person (he/his).
* **hers:** Possessive pronoun used without a noun (e.g., *the garden is hers*), whereas here it precedes the noun *grandfather*.
* **him:** Objective pronoun (e.g., *I saw him*), not a possessive modifier.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "her" as a possessive adjective before a noun for a female person (e.g., *her garden*, *her grandfather*).

sectionA.questionText: 17. Asha grows ----17---- vegetables in her garden.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Adjectives describe nouns. In the context of a vegetable garden, growing various types of crops is described using the adjective **different**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**different** is correct because it fits the context of growing various kinds of vegetables (such as spinach, kales, carrots).

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **dry:** Vegetables being grown in a garden are living and watered, not dry.
* **cooked:** Vegetables grow raw in a garden, not already cooked.
* **plenty:** "Plenty" is a noun/determiner used with "of" (*plenty of vegetables*), not a direct pre-modifier here.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** "Different vegetables" means various types of healthy crops growing in a garden.

sectionA.questionText: 18. She ----18---- taking care of her vegetables.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Verb selection relies on contextual meaning. The passage states Asha likes her garden and prefers working in it over sitting inside playing phone games.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**enjoys** is correct because it expresses her positive feeling and pleasure in taking care of her vegetables.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **begins:** Refers to starting an action, which does not express her love or passion for gardening.
* **accepts:** Means agreeing to something, which does not capture her joyful active participation.
* **admires:** Means looking at something with appreciation, whereas taking care requires active work (*enjoys taking care*).

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** "Enjoys taking care" shows active pleasure and dedication in maintaining a garden.

sectionA.questionText: 19. She does not like to sit in the house ----19---- play games on the phone.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Conjunctions connect words or clauses. The coordinating conjunction **and** is used to join two parallel negative activities that Asha dislikes doing together (*sit in the house AND play games on the phone*).

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**and** is correct because it smoothly joins the two linked indoor activities she avoids.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **also:** An adverb used for adding info, requiring a different sentence structure.
* **yet:** A contrasting conjunction meaning "but", which does not fit two parallel negative choices.
* **because:** A causal conjunction used to give a reason, not to join two parallel actions.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "and" to join two related actions or items in a sentence.

sectionA.questionText: 20. She hopes to sell her harvest ----20---- month.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Time expressions modify future expectations. The phrase "hopes to sell her harvest..." refers to a coming time period, expressed by the adjective **next**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**next** is correct because "next month" is the standard time expression for the upcoming month.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **future:** Used as a noun (*in the future*) or modifier (*future plans*), not directly as *future month*.
* **new:** Refers to something recently created, not a calendar time expression.
* **later:** An adverb (*sell it later*), requiring "later this month" rather than *later month*.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "next month" to refer to the month immediately following the present one.

sectionA.questionText: 21. The teacher found the learner ------- the classroom.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Prepositions of place show location. To indicate being enclosed inside a room or building, we use the preposition **in**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**in** is correct because a classroom is an enclosed space (*inside the classroom*).

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **to:** Indicates direction or movement towards a destination (*walking to the classroom*).
* **on:** Indicates resting on a flat surface (*on the table*).
* **over:** Indicates position above or higher than something (*over the roof*).

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "in" for enclosed locations like classrooms, rooms, and buildings.

sectionA.questionText: 22. Ali left the book ------- the table.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Prepositions of surface location describe where an object is resting. When an item rests on the top flat surface of furniture, we use **on**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**on** is correct because a book rests on top of the flat surface of a table.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **with:** Indicates companionship or instrument used.
* **in:** Means inside an enclosed space (e.g., *in the drawer*).
* **from:** Indicates source or origin (*from the library*).

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "on" when an object rests on a surface like a table, desk, or floor.

sectionA.questionText: 23. The children are planting trees, -------
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Question tags follow specific rules:
1. Positive statement ➔ Negative tag.
2. The statement uses auxiliary verb **are** and subject pronoun **they** (*The children* = *they*).
3. Therefore, the correct tag is **aren't they?**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**aren't they?** is correct because it matches the positive statement "The children are..." with a negative auxiliary and matching pronoun.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **aren't we?:** Changes the subject pronoun from 3rd person plural (*they*) to 1st person plural (*we*).
* **are they?:** Positive tag; a positive statement requires a negative tag.
* **are we?:** Positive tag with an incorrect subject pronoun.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Positive statement ➔ Negative tag matching subject and verb (*The children are... aren't they?*).

sectionA.questionText: 24. Rudisha did not find the story book in his bag because ------- had taken it.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Indefinite pronouns refer to unspecified persons:
- **Somebody / Someone**: Used in affirmative statements when a specific unknown person took an action.
- **Anybody**: Used in questions and negative statements.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**somebody** is correct because the clause "...because somebody had taken it" is an affirmative statement explaining an unknown thief/person.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **anybody:** Used in negative statements (*did not see anybody*) or questions (*did anybody take it?*).
* **everybody:** Means all people, which makes no sense as multiple people wouldn't take a single book.
* **nobody:** Means no person; saying "nobody took it" would contradict why the book was missing.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "somebody" in positive statement clauses to refer to an unknown person.

sectionA.questionText: 25. The teacher told us to take care of ------- during the journey.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Reflexive pronouns refer back to the subject of the sentence:
- Subject **us / we** ➔ Reflexive pronoun **ourselves**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**ourselves** is correct because the teacher told *us* (1st person plural) to take care of *ourselves*.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **themselves:** Reflexive pronoun for *they* (3rd person plural).
* **yourself:** Singular reflexive pronoun for *you* (2nd person singular).
* **yourselves:** Plural reflexive pronoun for *you all* (2nd person plural).

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Subject pronoun 'we / us' pairs with reflexive pronoun 'ourselves'.

sectionA.questionText: 26. The thieves took away our goats ------- force.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Prepositional phrases indicating manner or method use set expressions. The standard phrase meaning using physical compulsion or violence is **by force**.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**by** is correct because **by force** is the correct idiomatic phrase in English.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **with:** Used for instruments (*with a knife*), not in the phrase *by force*.
* **at:** Used for location or time, not manner of taking.
* **under:** Used in phrases like *under pressure* or *under arrest*, not *by force*.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** The correct idiomatic prepositional phrase is "by force".

sectionA.questionText: 27. This is the hen ------- egg broke.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Relative pronouns link clauses:
- **whose**: Shows possession for people, animals, or objects (*the hen whose egg broke*).
- **who / whom**: Used for human subjects/objects.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**whose** is correct because it shows possession (*the egg belonging to the hen*).

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **who:** Subject pronoun used for human beings (*the teacher who taught us*).
* **whom:** Object pronoun used for human beings (*the person whom I met*).
* **which:** Used for non-possessive references to animals/things (*the hen which laid an egg*).

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Use "whose" to show possession for people, animals, or objects.

sectionA.questionText: 28. The class teacher will ------- us a present.
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Modal auxiliary verbs (**will, shall, can, may, must, should, would**) are always followed by the **bare infinitive** (base form of the main verb without 'to').

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**give** is correct because the modal verb **will** takes the base verb form **give** (*will give*).

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **given:** Past participle form (*has given*), cannot follow modal *will* directly.
* **gives:** Third-person singular present form, cannot follow a modal verb.
* **gave:** Simple past tense form, cannot follow a modal verb.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Modal verbs (will, shall, can, may) MUST be followed by the base verb form (give).

sectionA.questionText:
29. 'Neither Kalusi nor Sofia came late to class'.
Means:

options.text: Only Kalusi came late to class.
Only Sofia came late to class.
Both Kalusi and Sofia came late to class.
Both Kalusi and Sofia did not come late to class.

sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Correlative conjunctions **Neither ... nor** mean "not the one and not the other" (negating both items mentioned).

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Both Kalusi and Sofia did not come late to class.** is correct because *neither... nor* means that neither student was late (both arrived on time).

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Only Kalusi came late to class.:** Incorrectly claims one student came late.
* **Only Sofia came late to class.:** Incorrectly claims the other student came late.
* **Both Kalusi and Sofia came late to class.:** Reverses the meaning into a positive statement of lateness for both.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** "Neither A nor B" means BOTH A and B did NOT perform or experience the action.

sectionA.questionText: 30. According to the story, who plays football only?
sectionA.explanation:
📘 **Study Note & Concept Overview:**
Reading logic matrices requires carefully checking every condition in the short passage:
- *Nasir*: plays football AND volleyball.
- *Banda*: plays football ONLY.
- *Lona*: plays football AND netball.

✅ **Correct Answer Breakdown:**
**Banda.** is correct because Banda plays football and has no other additional sport mentioned, making him the only one who plays football ONLY.

❌ **Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Nasir.:** Plays football AND volleyball.
* **Lona.:** Plays football AND netball.
* **All of them.:** All three play football, but Nasir and Lona play additional sports, so they do not play football *only*.

💡 **Key Takeaway for Revision:** Pay close attention to restrictive words like "only" when reading comprehension puzzles.

ctx-swa-q1-5.text:

**Leni:** (Akitabasamu.) Bingwa, hujambo? Ha! Ha! Ha! Umejitwika mtungi kichwani kutafuta maji!

**Kibo:** (Akionyesha kukasirika.) Sijambo, lakini mimi si bingwa. Ubingwa gani na hata tone la maji sina?

**Leni:** (Akionyesha kuhuzunika.) Ni kweli unavyosema mwenzangu. Lakini hiyo anga itabadilikaje ilhali miti inakatwa ovyo?

**Leni:** (Akikubaliana naye.) Tutajenga ukuta. Nasikitika hali hii ikiendelea tutakosa chakula. Wanyama na ndege nao watakosa makao.

ctx-swa-q6-9.text:
Ushuru ni malipo yanayotozwa na serikali kama ada ya kuingiza bidhaa ndani ya nchi au kuziuza nje ya nchi. Pia, ni ada inayotozwa raia kwa kuuza au kununua huduma mbalimbali. Nchi yetu hutegemea ushuru ambao wananchi hutozwa ili kuendesha shughuli zake.

Shirika lenye jukumu la kukusanya ushuru nchini Kenya ni Halmashauri ya Ukusanyaji Ushuru almaarufu KRA. Shirika hili limepewa mamlaka ya kikatiba kukusanya aina zote za ushuru: ushuru wa mapato, ushuru wa forodhani, ushuru kutokana na shughuli za kitalii na nyinginezo.

Serikali huandaa bajeti kila mwaka ili kuhakikisha matumizi yafaayo ya fedha. Bajeti huwa na makadirio ya mapato na mgao wa fedha kwa matumizi mbalimbali. Makadirio hayo husomwa bungeni na Waziri wa Hazina ya Kitaifa kisha **kuidhinishwa**.

Ni wajibu wa kila mwananchi kulipa ushuru ili taifa letu liweze kujitegemea. Tukifanya hivyo, tutaweza kupiga hatua kimaendeleo. Tutakuwa na miundomsingi bora, huduma nzuri za kimsingi kama vile afya na elimu na hata nafasi zaidi za ajira.

ctx-swa-q10-12.title:
Swali la 10 hadi la 12
Soma kifungu kifuatacho kisha ujibu maswali.
ctx-swa-q10-12.text:
Likizo iliyopita nilitumia muda wangu wa mapumziko kumsaidia mlezi wangu **kuwatunza** mifugo wetu. Jambo hilo lilimfurahisha sana mlezi wangu akanizawidi ndama wa kike. Nilimpa ndama wangu jina, Simati.

Nilijitolea kwa hali na mali kumtunza Simati. Anapendeza kwa rangi yake nyeupe na madoa meusi. Matarajio yangu ni kwamba siku za usoni atapata ndama wake. Wakati huo utakapofika, nitamkama maziwa.

Maziwa nitakayoyapata nitayagawa kwa matumizi ya nyumbani na mengine nitayauza kwa usaidizi wa mlezi wangu. Hela nitakazopata kutokana na mauzo ya maziwa hayo, nitaziweka kama akiba kwani akiba haiozi.

ctx-swa-q13-15.title:
Swali la 13 hadi la 15
